remove: The back's 'Star size: Iowa accounts pouring the brand (PHG brand graph)' legend and the dot-size system. It is internal sales data dressed up as a star atlas. Guests cannot use it, it adds a third code (dot, +, square) on top of the proposed-ring key, and it turns the spirits list into a dashboard. The hand-drawn glass glyphs are the next device to cut: tiny clip-art icons with red and brown liquid fills that compete with the names.
top_problem: The concept is split in two, and neither half is rooted in Mexico. The front's dusk dial is a real, ownable piece of geometry: the rim, the 5-minute ticks and the stepped blocks work together. But a gold-to-indigo 'golden hour' gradient is a stock sunset trope that could front any rooftop bar in any city. The back drops the dial for a different idea (a log-scale oak ladder plus a star atlas) that leaves two large dead fields on the page. What the design lacks is one image system with cultural materiality. Solstice and The Bistro stand on texture, collage and gold leaf with a single illustration grammar. K2 is flat vector gradient on flat cream, with no paper, ink or print texture, no Mexican craft reference, and no Iowa beyond the word 'Iowa' in 'Iowa wildflower honey'. Next to the references it reads as a smart infographic, not a menu you can't forget. That is 70-75 on concept, not 85.
fixes: Carry the dial onto the back: continue the rim and graduation from 12 am to 2 am down the page and hang the spirits by age class along that same arc. This replaces the separate oak ladder, removes the two empty log-gap fields, and makes front and back one concept.

Give the image system a material and a place: render the dusk field as a textured print (for example a risograph or serigraph grain, or Oaxacan cochineal-to-indigo dye tones) with texture that drops to flat under text. The gradient then reads as Mexican craft rather than a UI sunset, and it passes the substitution test.

Bring the hour numerals to their drinks: put a short gold leader or hairline from each hour tick to the name row, or set a small hour tag at each cluster's left edge, so the clock visibly times the drinks instead of floating 150-400 pt away.

Set zero proof on the stepped arc (or on the 36 pt margin) and give its 'Sin alcohol' head the same level, size and x rule as 'Cócteles'. Then close the Manhattan and Carajillo holes by pairing them with zero-proof items at their hours, so the bottom band is no longer empty.

Use one price format throughout (all whole numbers with 11.50 shown as a deliberate superscript 50, or all to two decimals), and cut the guest-facing Iowa-account dots and the 'PHG brand graph' caption from the back.

lens: every item and price vs expanded-v1/manifest.json

The weakness is the concept itself. The sun-clock and months-in-oak axes put PHG inferences into print that the manifest does not support, and they cost the menu its structure. The manifest's Clásicos / De la Casa split is gone, so no guest can tell the house signatures (Milpa, Loess, Brown Butter OF) from the classics. Hour placements the proposal itself calls 'PHG-inferred, not manifest data' face the guest. The chart puts all four mezcals on the 0-month 'unaged' rung, but the manifest says unaged only for Ilegal Joven, and the proposal says 'verify before print'. Open manifest flags print as if they were settled facts: the Brut Rosé 'glass or bottle unknown (needs_input 5)' price of 13 sits in the 'Por copa · By the glass' column, the three mezcal 'PRICE PLACEHOLDER' prices ($12, $13, $10) look final (the ring only says 'proposed'), and Spicy Pineapple's 'confirm liqueur/citrus' is not flagged.
problems: Brut Rosé 13 is printed under the 'Por copa · By the glass' head with no pour label, but the manifest says glass or bottle is unknown (needs_input 5), so the menu implies a glass price nobody has confirmed.
Montelobos Espadín 12, Ilegal Joven 13 and 400 Conejos Espadín 10 are manifest PRICE PLACEHOLDERs. They carry only the generic 'proposed' ring, so they look like real prices.
The manifest groups Clásicos · Classics and De la Casa · House were dropped without a note. Cocktails are regrouped by inferred hour, so the house signatures have no identity.

Mezcal sits in a chart headed 'Twenty-five pours, set by months in oak' at the 0-month rung. That prints an 'unaged' class for Del Maguey Vida, Montelobos and 400 Conejos, but the manifest states it only for Ilegal Joven.

Section order is cocktails, then zero proof (hung at 'midnight' on the cocktail page), then spirits, then beer, cider and wine packed into the bottom band of the back. Wine gets three lines under 25 spirits and is not treated as an equal drinks category.
The back chart leaves large empty bands (6–12 and 24–36 months) as data-driven dead space, while beer, cider and wine are crowded into the last 20% of the page.

The front reading path is ambiguous: the paired hour rows zigzag and step right along the rim, so the eye cannot tell whether to read across a row or down a column. Manhattan sits alone at 9 pm and breaks the pairs.

Give the three placeholder mezcal prices and the Spicy Pineapple recipe a distinct flag (for example '◦ price TBC' or 'recipe TBC') separate from the approval ring, and state the 1.5 oz pour once at the head of the spirits page.

Restore the Clásicos / De la Casa grouping inside the hour structure (for example a small 'Casa' marker on the four house signatures), or move the hour placements to staff notes as the proposal's open question 1 suggests.

Take mezcal off the months-in-oak axis (set it as its own off-scale block headed 'Mezcal espadín · Oaxaca') unless Rob confirms all four are jóvenes, and change the subhead so it no longer says all 25 pours are set by oak.

lens: Voice and consistency of descriptions, bilingual headings and venue copy, and fit to a Mexican restaurant and cocktail bar in Iowa City

All 50 names and prices match expanded-v1/manifest.json (gates.json DOM diff 50/50). All PROPOSED and rob_reference_image rows carry the ring and the key is on both pages. Criterion 9 is clean.
Price format is mixed: Ranch Water is printed '11.50' and every other price is a whole number, so decimals appear once on the page.

The manifest's cocktail groups 'Clásicos · Classics' and 'De la Casa · House' are dropped. The house signatures (Loess, Milpa Old Fashioned, Brown Butter Old Fashioned) can no longer be told apart from the classics, so the venue's own drinks lose their emphasis.

Zero proof (4 items) prints only a sensory line: no ingredients, no glass and no missing_ingredients flag. Voice drift: the cocktail sensory lines are crafted ('Soft smoke, honey, ginger snap'), but the beer and wine lines are taxonomy that repeats the category ('Dry white wine', 'Dry sparkling cider', 'Crisp pale lager'). 'Mexican fruit soda; ask for flavors' switches to a staff instruction with a semicolon. The back reads as a different writer.

Venue copy is off-register for guests: 'Star size: Iowa accounts pouring the brand (PHG brand graph)' and the NOM numbers as a 'catalogue designation' are distributor and industry data, not cantina hospitality. 'PHG brand graph' is internal jargon on a printed menu.

Beer, cider and wine are compressed into a footer band under a 25-pour chart. For an Iowa City cantina where Modelo and Tecate are high-volume, that under-weights a core category.

Reading path on the back: the ladder leaves large empty runs (the 6-12 and 24-36 month zones) while beer and wine are cramped at the bottom. Emphasis goes to the chart's geometry, not to what guests order.

Replace 'Star size: Iowa accounts pouring the brand (PHG brand graph)' with guest language (for example 'Larger star: poured more widely across Iowa') or move the star data to the staff edition, and drop 'PHG brand graph' from the guest menu.

Flag missing_ingredients for the zero-proof drinks and ask for them, and ask for ABV for each beer and region for each wine. Then rewrite the beer, wine and cider sensory lines in the cocktails' three-beat voice from those sourced facts, never from invented ones.

Print Ranch Water as '11.5'-free consistent format by confirming a whole-number price with Rob or by showing all prices with two decimals. Also restore a quiet 'De la Casa' marker for Loess, Milpa and Brown Butter so the house drinks stay distinguishable inside the hour arc.

Standardise the bilingual heads to italic Spanish · roman English everywhere (for example 'Tequila blanco', 'Mezcal espadín', 'Coñac · Cognac VSOP'). Take zero proof off the midnight hour and give beer, cider and wine a full-width band equal in weight to the other categories.

lens: Every printed ingredient, garnish, glass, NOM and region traced to expanded-v1/manifest.json, phg.recipe_versions and public.brands.primary_nom. Also judged the Iowa-accounts star sizing on the back page.
top_problem: All the printed text traces to its source. The two data graphics on the back do not. (1) The legend says 'Star size: Iowa accounts pouring the brand' and the proposal claims star area is proportional to the count. build.py line 212 actually uses r = 1.3 + 3.9*sqrt(n/1288) pt, and the 1.3 pt floor breaks that. Measured on preview-back.png, the legend discs for 100 / 500 / 1,000 are 19 / 31 / 39 px across, so their areas run 1 : 2.5 : 4.1 when the data runs 1 : 5 : 10. Patron Silver (1288) against Tres Generaciones (82) prints as 5.7:1 by area when the true ratio is 15.7:1. (2) The 'Months in oak' axis puts all four mezcals on the 0-month rung. The manifest states 'Unaged' only for Ilegal Joven, and the proposal itself says 'Verify before print'. Each pour row also sits at a height on a quantitative log axis. That implies a per-bottle age nobody sourced: Milagro Silver reads at 1 month, Teremana at about 4 months, Tres Generaciones at about 15 months. So the back page prints data claims that the data does not support.

verified.approved_cocktails_vs_phg.recipe_version: All match (case normalised to lowercase in print, which is acceptable). Margarita rv f06abb74: Rocks / Lime wheel. Manhattan rv 9fb77eaa: Coupe / Cocktail cherry. House Daiquiri rv 14d45e57: Coupe / Lime coin. Brown Butter Old Fashioned rv 7095fd3d: Rocks / Orange peel. My component join returned nothing. verified.proposed_and_ref_cocktails_vs_manifest: Ingredients, garnish and glass all match the manifest verbatim for Paloma, Ranch Water, Batanga, Carajillo (no garnish, correctly omitted), Mezcal Negroni, Spicy Pineapple Margarita (no garnish; the manifest's 'confirm liqueur/citrus' is covered by the ring), Milpa Old Fashioned and Loess. Every one carries the ring key.
verified.NOM_vs_public.brands.primary_nom: All 17 printed NOMs match. Espolon 1440, Olmeca Altos 1111, Milagro 1559, Patron 1492, Siete Leguas 1120, Casamigos 1609, Don Julio 1449 (brand 'Don Julio 1942' is also 1449), Hornitos 1102, Cazadores 1487, Teremana 1613, Corralejo 1368, Herradura 1119, Fortaleza 1493, Clase Azul 1595, Tres Generaciones 1102, El Tesoro 1139. Casa Noble has brand primary_nom null, and the design correctly prints no NOM (the 1137 row belongs to 'Marques de Casa Noble' / 'Cn Casa Noble', so it was rightly not borrowed).
verified.regions_vs_manifest: Los Altos, Tequila Valley, Guanajuato and Oaxaca are printed only where the manifest has them, and none were added. Two caveats. The manifest's region_note says 'verify before print'. Hornitos and Tres Generaciones share NOM 1102, yet only Tres Generaciones gets 'Tequila Valley', because Hornitos' region is null in the manifest. verified.glyphs: Every glass glyph matches its manifest glass: rocks, highball or coupe. Every garnish cue matches its manifest garnish. Red liquid appears only on the Campari drink and dark liquid only on the cola and espresso drinks. No invented cue.

star_sizing_judgement: The stars fail as data graphics and are doubtful on a guest menu. (a) The sizes are not proportional. A radius floor compresses the range about 2.5x, so 130 (Herradura, 21 px) and 490 (Casamigos, 31 px) look like neighbours. Either use true area (r proportional to sqrt(n) with no offset) or change the legend to say the scale is compressed. (b) The legend promises brand-level counts, but Don Julio Blanco gets a large disc (946) while Don Julio 1942 gets '+ no data'. The graph keys 'Don Julio 1942' as a separate brand. A guest reads Don Julio as one brand and will see a contradiction. (c) The marks are discs, not stars, so 'Star size' in the legend does not describe what is on the page. (d) Venue fit: 'Iowa accounts pouring the brand (PHG brand graph)' is distributor sales-graph language. Next to a name, a disc reads as a rating or popularity badge. The result is that mass well brands get large discs (Hornitos 650, Teremana 851) while craft tequilas (Fortaleza, Siete Leguas, El Tesoro) and all the mezcals get '+ no data'. That tells an Iowa City guest the prestige bottles are the unknowns. (e) The back now carries four mark systems per row (disc, +, house square, proposed ring) plus the price. That is too much noise at 8.5 pt. Recommendation: make the stars staff-only (Rob's open question 4) and drop them from the guest print and phone versions.

lens: Descriptions and prices laid out together in the K2 'El Reloj' print PNGs (preview-front.png, preview-back.png), plus the price-to-item association gate
top_problem: On the back, Ilegal Joven's own sensory line ('Unaged, pit-roasted · smoke, citrus peel') is set in the same italic as the class-sensory heads and sits directly above 400 Conejos Espadín. The page's own rule is that an italic line describes what comes below it, so the line reads as 400 Conejos' description. That is a description attached to the wrong item, and it fails menu_item_association. gates.json checks only price-to-name gaps (letter_price_pairs max_gap_em 0.42, all_same_line true), so it cannot catch this. Prices are well tied to their names everywhere: inline, gold, on the same line. The layout still loses points because the front ingredient lines break inside compound ingredients and leave orphans: 'sparkling / mineral water' (Ranch Water), 'grapefruit / soda' (Paloma), 'Mexican / cola' (Batanga), 'agave / syrup' (Margarita), 'sweet / vermouth' (Mezcal Negroni), 'house / demerara syrup' (Brown Butter Old Fashioned), and a lone 'ginger' (Loess) and a lone 'bitters' (Brown Butter Old Fashioned) on their own last lines. No spirit pour or wine glass shows a pour size, and beers show no size or ABV. On content integrity, every printed fact traces to expanded-v1/manifest.json, so the gate passes. But three items are only inferences, and manifest.region_note itself says 'verify before print': the regions ('Los Altos', 'Tequila Valley', 'Oaxaca'), the mezcal pours sitting on the 0-months-in-oak rung (proposal.md line 73), and the drink-hour assignments (gates.json hours_phg_inferred). Other notes. The star legend 'Iowa accounts pouring the brand (PHG brand graph)' is internal market data shown to guests (manifest.iowa_basis = public.v_brand_geography_presence), which hurts venue fit. Several descriptions read as category labels or just restate the name: 'Dry red wine', 'Dry white wine', 'Hop-forward draft IPA', 'Crisp pale lager', 'Dry sparkling cider'. The zero-proof drinks have no ingredient line and no garnish · glass line, which breaks Rob's item stack. On the front, Manhattan (9 pm) and Carajillo (11 pm) each sit alone with an empty column beside them. Ranch Water is the only price with decimals (11.50). I sent no Supabase queries. The review used only the manifest named in PANEL_K_INSTRUCTIONS.md, and the phone PNG was not inspected because of the tool-call limit.

Rebalance the ingredient measure or use non-breaking spaces inside compound ingredients (sparkling mineral water, grapefruit soda, Mexican cola, agave syrup, sweet vermouth, house demerara syrup), so no ingredient splits across lines and 'ginger' and 'bitters' are not left alone on a line.
Label pours: add a single 'pours 1.5 oz' note to the Destilados head (manifest.pour_size, marked proposed), and put pour sizes on the wine-by-the-glass rows and serve sizes plus ABV on the beers.

Mark NOM regions, the mezcal 0-month placement and the drink hours as pending verification (regions were filled by the design lead, per manifest.region_note), and move the Iowa-accounts star legend to a staff-only version or turn it into a guest-facing line.

lens: Descriptions and prices together on the phone PNG (preview-phone.png, 1170x14532, cropped into 4 slices; slices 2 and 3 inspected: 9 pm to 12 am cocktails, zero proof, blanco, mezcal, reposado)
top_problem: On the phone the hour rail takes about 18% of the width, and the rail edge sits another 70 px from the text. That leaves the ingredient line about 30 characters wide, so ingredient names break in the middle. Examples: 'rye whiskey · sweet / vermouth' (Manhattan), 'house roasted-corn / syrup' (Milpa OF), 'house / demerara syrup · aromatic / bitters' (Brown Butter OF). The garnish and glass then run into the same line as the ingredients, marked only by italic, so the cocktail above the Manhattan reads 'ginger  candied ginger · rocks'. Prices themselves are fine: gold, inline, one space after the name, no eye travel. Facts I checked against manifest.json: Manhattan = rye whiskey, sweet vermouth, cocktail cherry, coupe (approved_db, rv 9fb77eaa). Brown Butter OF = brown butter-washed bourbon, house demerara syrup, aromatic bitters, orange peel, rocks (rv 7095fd3d). Carajillo = Licor 43, fresh espresso, rocks, no garnish (PROPOSED, ringed). Espolòn is spelled with the grave accent, as in the manifest. Casa Noble has nom null and region null, so it correctly has no second line. Zero-proof items are PROPOSED or rob_reference_image and ringed. Every printed fact traces, and the 5 pm to 2 am hours are disclosed as a PHG suggestion. Remaining problems: (a) the ring key says 'proposed — pending approval', but Nojito and Jarritos are rob_reference_image, not proposals; (b) the ring key is printed only once, above Destilados, yet about 25 spirit rings follow it with no key on the phone; (c) zero proof is placed at 12 am, which suggests non-alcoholic drinks are a last-call afterthought, a poor fit for a college-town cantina where N/A drinks are ordered all evening; (d) the empty Casa Noble second line leaves a visible hole in an otherwise even row rhythm; (e) the Mezcal espadín head repeats the '0 months' rung label, and 'Ilegal Joven' prints its own sensory line under 'Oaxaca', so that row has a different stack from its neighbours.
fixes: Designer note: on the phone, cut the hour rail to about 90 px and shrink the rail-to-text gap to 24 px so the ingredient measure reaches about 40 characters, and keep each ingredient together on one line (non-breaking spaces inside names like 'sweet vermouth' and 'demerara syrup').
Designer note: put 'garnish · glass' on its own line under the ingredients, per Rob's stack line 4, so a garnish never shares a line with ingredients (fixes 'ginger  candied ginger · rocks').

Change the key to two statuses, or reword it to 'proposed or reference item — pending approval', so Nojito and Jarritos (rob_reference_image) are not mislabelled, and repeat the key once at the head of Destilados on the phone.
Move Sin alcohol · Zero proof out of the 12 am slot (for example beside the 5 pm or 6 pm opener, or as its own untimed band), because N/A drinks should read as all-evening for this venue.
Give rows with no NOM or region (Casa Noble Reposado) a fixed-height second line or compress the row, so the reposado list keeps an even rhythm.
